name: Find low-CTR pages in Search Console and rewrite titles with OpenAI and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Find low-CTR pages in Search Console and rewrite their titles with AI

### How it works

Every week this workflow pulls page performance from Google Search Console and flags pages whose CTR is well below what their average position should earn (a position-based CTR benchmark). Pages are ranked by **missed clicks** (impressions × CTR gap). For each page it fetches the **top search queries for that page** and the **live title, meta description and H1**, then an LLM writes a new SEO title, an alternative title and a meta description aimed at those real queries. Every suggestion lands in Google Sheets as `pending` with a length check.

Review the sheet, edit if you like, and set `status` to `approved`. If write-back is enabled, the hourly run updates the post's SEO title and meta description in WordPress (Yoast or Rank Math). Otherwise approved rows are marked `manual` so you can paste them yourself.

### Setup steps

- **Search Console:** create a **Google OAuth2 API** credential with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly` and select it in the three Search Console HTTP nodes.
- **Google Sheets:** create a tab named `SEO Log` with this header row:
`page_url | wp_id | wp_type | impressions | clicks | ctr | position | expected_ctr | missed_clicks | top_queries | current_title | current_description | new_title | alt_title | new_description | rationale | length_check | status | updated_at`
- **AI model:** add OpenAI credentials, or swap the chat model for Claude, Gemini or another model.
- **WordPress:** create an Application Password and a WordPress API credential for the lookup and write-back nodes.
- **Config:** set `gsc_property` (e.g. `sc-domain:example.com` or `https://example.com/`), `wp_base_url`, `sheet_id` and `language`.
- Run **On-Demand Activation** once with `max_per_run = 3` and check the sheet.

### Optional: write back to Yoast / Rank Math

Set `seo_plugin` to `yoast` or `rank_math` and add this snippet as a must-use plugin, so the SEO fields become writable through the REST API:

```php
<?php
// wp-content/mu-plugins/n8n-seo-meta.php
add_action('init', function () {
  $keys = ['_yoast_wpseo_title', '_yoast_wpseo_metadesc',
           'rank_math_title', 'rank_math_description'];
  foreach (['post', 'page'] as $type) {
    foreach ($keys as $key) {
      register_post_meta($type, $key, [
        'show_in_rest'  => true,
        'single'        => true,
        'type'          => 'string',
        'auth_callback' => fn() => current_user_can('edit_posts'),
      ]);
    }
  }
});
```

Test on a staging site first and confirm the new title appears in the page source.

### Customization

- `min_impressions`, `max_position` and `ctr_ratio` control which pages count as underperforming.
- For Japanese, Chinese or Korean sites, lower `max_title_length` to about 32 and `max_description_length` to about 120.
- `cooldown_days` stops a page from being suggested again before the change has had time to show results.
- The CTR benchmark curve lives in **Calculate Underperformance Score**. Replace it with your own site's averages for better accuracy.

## Trigger and route run

Starts the workflow from weekly, hourly, or manual triggers, sets shared configuration values, and routes execution into either suggestion generation or approved-row application.

## Load SEO performance

Reads the existing SEO log from Google Sheets and fetches recent page performance data from Google Search Console.

## Score weak pages

Ranks pages by missed-click opportunity using a position-based CTR benchmark to identify the best title rewrite candidates.

## Match WordPress content

Looks up matching WordPress posts and pages by slug, then attaches the relevant WordPress IDs and content type to each candidate URL.

## Collect page context

Fetches top Search Console queries for each page, retrieves the live page HTML, and extracts the current title and meta description.

## Generate AI suggestions

Uses an OpenAI chat model with structured output parsing to rewrite the SEO title and description, then formats the suggestion fields for logging.

## Log generated suggestions

Writes the generated title and meta description suggestions to Google Sheets for review and approval.

## Read approved rows

Loads approved suggestions from Google Sheets and checks whether each row has enough WordPress information to be applied automatically.

## Apply or flag updates

Updates SEO metadata in WordPress for eligible approved rows, marks successful rows as applied in Google Sheets, or marks rows for manual handling when automatic write-back is not possible.
